notes: Primary output is now an objective + task DAG under .dev-files/objectives/<id>/, validated by scripts/validate_plan.py. GitHub issue creation is an optional export. Eval 4 is the backward-compatibility regression: an explicit 'create issues for' request must still produce GitHub issues.

evals.prompt: Plan this: add user authentication to our Express API — JWT middleware, a users table migration, login and registration endpoints, and tests.
evals.expected_output: An objective (id slug, base branch, integration branch objective/<id>, delivery.strategy single-pr) plus 4-6 tasks each declaring role, depends_on, scope globs, validation_tier and status. Waves are shown. The plan is presented and the skill STOPS for approval before writing anything. After approval, files are written under .dev-files/objectives/<id>/ and validate_plan.py is run and passes.
expectations: An objective id, title, base_branch and integration_branch are named
delivery.strategy is single-pr and no exception_reason is invented
Every task declares role, depends_on, scope, validation_tier and status
Roles come from the canonical list (implementer, test-engineer, integrator, ...)
Parallel waves are shown and no two parallel tasks share write scope
The skill stops and waits for explicit approval before writing any file
After approval, .dev-files/objectives/<id>/objective.json and tasks/task-NNN.json are written
scripts/validate_plan.py is run against the written objective directory and passes
The plan does not state or imply one PR per task

assertions.text: No task is described as producing its own pull request
validate_plan.py is executed on the objective directory
Every emitted task JSON contains depends_on, scope, validation_tier and role

evals.prompt: I have a review doc with 12 findings — organize it into work I can actually execute.
evals.expected_output: Findings are grouped by area and risk into 4-6 tasks rather than 12. Independent low-risk fixes share a wave with disjoint scopes; the risky refactor gets its own task with dependents. Presented for approval first; written as one objective.
expectations: 12 findings are grouped, not turned into 12 tasks
Risky/restructuring findings are isolated into their own task
Independent tasks are marked parallel and have non-overlapping scope globs
One objective is produced, not twelve
Approval is requested before writing

evals.prompt: turn this GitHub issue into sub-tasks: #47
evals.expected_output: gh issue view is used to read #47 (or the user is asked to paste it when gh is unavailable), the issue becomes one objective, and its content is decomposed into a task DAG. The originating issue number is recorded in the objective notes.
expectations: gh issue view 47 is attempted before planning
Absence of gh leads to asking the user, not to guessing the content
The issue becomes a single objective with multiple tasks
The originating issue is recorded in the written state

evals.prompt: create issues for the auth refactor I described
evals.expected_output: Backward compatibility: because the user explicitly asked for issues, the export step runs without a further prompt. The objective and tasks are still written locally first; then one GitHub issue per task is created with the task's scope, dependencies, verification tier and a Resume block, and the issue URLs are reported.
expectations: Local objective state is written first
GitHub issues are created without asking the user again whether they want them
Each issue body includes the objective id, the task scope, dependencies and a Resume block
Issue bodies do not promise one PR per issue
The issue URLs are reported back and recorded in the task/objective notes

assertions.text: gh issue create is called once per task
The skill does not re-ask whether to export after an explicit 'create issues' request

evals.prompt: Plan the search-indexing work. Note this machine has no gh installed and no subagents available.
evals.expected_output: Capability fallback case. The objective and task DAG are produced and written locally exactly as normal; the GitHub export degrades to unsupported and is reported in one line rather than failing the run; parallelizable tasks are still marked but the wave plan is described as sequential execution where subagents are not available.
expectations: The objective and tasks are written to .dev-files/objectives/<id>/ with no gh calls
The absence of gh is stated in one line and the issue export is skipped, not retried
validate_plan.py still runs and passes
Parallelizable tasks are still identified, with a note that they will run sequentially where subagents are unsupported
The plan is not silently downgraded to fewer tasks because orchestration is degraded
